key_insight: SpecFirst argues that building programs from scratch should start with explicit behavioral specification elicitation, not immediate code synthesis. By separating understanding the task from generating code, agent-based systems can better handle extremely sparse or execute-only problem settings.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the difficulty of synthesizing software from scratch when agents only have natural-language documentation and an execute-only binary as a behavioral oracle. It tackles the failure mode where current LLM agents mix documentation reading, exploration, and synthesis in one pass, leading to very low success rates.
method: Split the workflow into distinct stages: specification elicitation first, then synthesis.
Use agent-driven behavioral exploration to infer how the target program should behave before coding.
Treat the specification as a first-class artifact that guides downstream program generation and reduces guesswork.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more reliable pipeline for program synthesis in low-context environments. It provides a practical design principle for improving agent performance on hard software-engineering benchmarks like ProgramBench.
